bluehat-podcast.title: A Must-Listen for Cybersecurity Enthusiasts
bluehat-podcast.content:
Nick Fillingham and Wendy Zenone bring a fantastic balance to the BlueHat Podcast. Nick’s deep knowledge and Wendy’s relatable style create an engaging and accessible show that resonates with listeners of all backgrounds. I noticed a prior review suggesting that one of the hosts was “out of place,” which felt both harsh and unhelpful. Constructive feedback is great, but I think both hosts add a fresh and valuable perspective that enhances the podcast’s accessibility and dynamic nature.

The production quality is top-notch, the topics are insightful, and the interviews are always on point. Whether you’re in the industry or just interested in the evolving tech landscape, this podcast is a goldmine of information. Highly recommend!

Thank you for the effort y’all put into these and what you’re doing for our community.

ciso-tradecraft.title: Critical Information for Our Critical Infrastructure
ciso-tradecraft.content:
The nature of the internet makes it incumbent on every organization to prevent intrusions, be they foreign or domestic. Corporate cybersecurity is not a business concern. It is a national Security concern.

For this reason, the information conveyed in this podcast should be on every cybersecurity professional’s listening list , from CISO to entry level security associateS just beginning their career.

There is no unimportant person when it comes to cybersecurity. Anyone who uses a computer connected to the internet can reign down catastrophe on an organization. It is up to cybersecurity personnel to prevent that from happening. G. Mark Hardy seems almost chosen to be the one that helps corporations stay safe. 

It doesn’t hurt that he has a calm, reassuring, voice that conveys a message that this is doable, and that you are the one who can do it.
ciso-tradecraft.author: PBinNewJ

ciso-tradecraft.title: A great resource for those in the cyber world

hacked.title: Great Hooks. Lacks Depth and Insight
hacked.content:
I first came across Hacked through their episode The Red Teamer, which was fantastic. The guest, a red teamer turned entrepreneur, shared insightful experiences from the industry and discussed the shift toward identity-based security. As a security professional, I found it fascinating to hear about real-world vulnerabilities and how attacks have evolved over time. This episode had depth, a great guest, and valuable takeaways—exactly what I was looking for.

Encouraged by that episode, I started exploring more of the podcast. Unfortunately, I found a disappointing pattern. While the show excels at drawing listeners in with strong hooks and compelling intros, the rest of the episode often turns into surface-level discussion rather than deep analysis. It feels like two guys casually chatting about cybersecurity news rather than breaking down attacks in a meaningful way.

A great example of this was the Ticketmaster breach episode. The intro set high expectations, making it seem like we’d get a well-researched breakdown of how two different groups exploited Ticketmaster—one stealing millions of barcodes, the other reverse-engineering the SafeTix algorithm. But instead of diving into the technical details, the episode quickly veered into a broad discussion about Ticketmaster’s reputation, its secondary market monopoly, and general opinions on the company. There was little to no real analysis of the breach itself—no insight into attack methods, security takeaways, or how the industry might respond to such threats.

Overall, Hacked has potential, but it needs more substance. If the hosts focused on deeper research—examining the technical aspects of attacks, lessons learned, and industry implications—this could be an excellent podcast. Right now, it too often feels like commentary on security headlines rather than an informative deep dive. I’m giving it 2 out of 5 stars because, while I really enjoyed The Red Teamer, the lack of meaningful analysis in other episodes left me frustrated. I hope the hosts consider adding more depth to their discussions in the future.

lock-and-code.title: Excellent history and overview of Macs and Malware
lock-and-code.content: I was using UNIX in 1978 and continued for over 40 years.  People who ran the computer network in Electrical Engineering at Purdue were very interested in malware, worms as I recall, as they first appeared on the scene and popped up on occasion. I was at a electronics show in Huston, TX in the early 80s and went with the head of our computer network to Xerox and saw/used the first mouse, so I was impressed when I saw the Macs and had to have one. I too thought the Mac was virus proof, assuming the propriety nature of the of the software and difficulty sharing software kept it safe, but when OS X came and the internet blossomed I knew that the UNIX based OS was vulnerable. I loved being able to get to the command line and continue using it even today, though not nearly as often.  I still imagine that the popularity of Windows and its vulnerabilities makes it a bigger target, but in reality with the complexity of todays software I see how important it is to use Malwarebytes to protect the Apple devices our family has.

nexus-claroty.title: A Must-Listen for ICS OT Cybersecurity Professionals and Enthusiasts Alike!
nexus-claroty.content:
I recently tuned into this podcast episode about the evolving landscape of PLC security, particularly focusing on the integration of embedded web servers, and I was thoroughly impressed. The host skillfully navigated the complex subject matter, making it accessible and engaging for listeners of all backgrounds. What stood out to me was the in-depth discussion on how these technological advancements, while beneficial in many ways, have opened up new vulnerabilities within industrial control systems. The conversation around the shift from traditional physical attacks to more sophisticated web-based strategies was eye-opening. It was fascinating to learn about the potential for these vulnerabilities to be exploited and the implications for both the IT and operational technology sectors.

The guest expert provided a balanced view, acknowledging the advancements in functionality and convenience brought by web-based interfaces, while also highlighting the critical need for improved security measures. Their insights into the detection challenges and the collaborative efforts between vendors and asset owners to mitigate risks added valuable depth to the discussion.

This episode not only shed light on a crucial issue facing the industry but did so in a way that was both informative and captivating. I came away with a much greater appreciation for the complexities of PLC security and the ongoing efforts to protect critical infrastructure. The podcast's ability to delve into such technical topics without losing the interest of the audience is commendable. I'm eagerly awaiting future episodes and highly recommend this podcast to anyone interested in the intersection of technology and security

Highly recommend listening and subscribing!

the-social-engineer-podcast.content:

It inspired me to write a review, buy the book sapiens, and download the app. My close friends and family tell me I have a way with people and I’ve never encountered before they talk about your podcast all the time and I believe that I would make a great SE. Thank You please keep up the hard work
Marco

the-social-engineer-podcast.content:
The Social Engineer Podcast (and movement) brings it back to the human element. This is critical as we see more and more the rise of AI/ML and more tech that takes humans out of the equation.

Humans are and will always be there, and we need to acknowledge that!

Keep it up!

to-the-point-cybersecurity.title: Amazing tech-forward podcast!
to-the-point-cybersecurity.content: To the point cybersecurity is a must-listen for anyone who wants to deepen their knowledge in cybersecurity! Each episode is engaging and dynamic, with hosts and guests who know how to captivate their audience.
to-the-point-cybersecurity.author: Erin13456

to-the-point-cybersecurity.title: A Must-Listen Podcast
to-the-point-cybersecurity.content: As someone still fairly new to the world of cybersecurity, To The Point Cybersecurity has been my secret ingredient in building the knowledge I need to stay ahead in the field. Each episode is engaging, featuring smart guests, timely topics, and hosts who know how to get to the heart of what matters most. I highly recommend To The Point to anyone who wants to sharpen their cyber skills!
to-the-point-cybersecurity.author: TechRunner14

to-the-point-cybersecurity.title: Great guest list
to-the-point-cybersecurity.content: While I have been featured on the show in a couple of episodes, I really appreciate all of the guests that to the point pulls in. People like Josh Corman, Nick Chaillan, Mishi Choudhary, and Chris Krebs are top in their class. I love that the episodes are full of great insight about cyber security issues, and that they are not just going for trying to promote forcepoint’s business. Kudos to the forcepoint team for pulling off years of high-quality content on a consistent basis.
to-the-point-cybersecurity.author: derekeweeks

to-the-point-cybersecurity.title: Timely and educational
to-the-point-cybersecurity.content: To The Point has been a very helpful resource for staying on top of cyber news and building my overall understanding of the major trends. The real-world stories of incident and response across industries are engaging and educational, which keeps me coming back!
to-the-point-cybersecurity.author: Imapersonto

to-the-point-cybersecurity.title: Full circle moment for Sunburst incident
to-the-point-cybersecurity.content: As someone who has been following along with To The Point for the last two years, I loved listening to Sudhakar Ramakrishna’s recent episode as it came full circle with his first episode recorded right after the Sunburst incident. Sudhakar’s transparency about the incident is refreshing and should stand as an example for how cybersecurity leaders should approach their organization’s missteps and the occasional crisis. I also hope that his “community vigil” mindset is an approach to cybersecurity that we see more of in the future.
to-the-point-cybersecurity.author: EmilyPMB223344

unsupervised-learning.title: UL podcast review
unsupervised-learning.content: I have a great time listening to this podcast. It is just an overview of the newsletter, but I often don’t find the time to read it. So I like to pick up the highlights that catch my interest and check them out later. This is one of the best technology oriented podcasts made today and there is a clear mission to help humanity via technological means. It is a mix of data (news, articles, etc), insights (putting disparate puzzle pieces close to each other), and thought leadership (educated opinions) that often brings together many of the work items I am interested in. Listen in, decide for yourself.
unsupervised-learning.author: Pedro-rocha

unsupervised-learning.title: Good until he injects politics into the discussion
unsupervised-learning.content: The podcast is a great source of information related to AI how it affects cyber security and life in general. What turned me off is he uses it to inject his political views along with it. I don’t care if the politics align with mine. If I wanted to hear about politics I’d be subscribing to a political podcast but I don’t want to hear about it. Unsubscribed
